points.text: Wrong figure references and notation typo.
Criteria for selecting attacker checkpoints for diverse strategies unclear.
Problem setup unrealistic; leakage avoidable by not giving user information to model.
Claim of enhanced task success unsupported; gains stem from imitation learning, capability drops.
Task success under attack conflates leakage with capability; benign task success not reported.
Imitation learning warm-up stage questionable; stronger base models would be fairer.
Improvements over ART baseline marginal or negative.
No ethics statement or reproducibility section.
Limited novelty; combines known self-play, GRPO and population-based training.
Only synthetic web environments; no real-world security gains shown.
Small gains lack statistical justification.
Attack diversity measured only by embedding distance.
No qualitative analysis of emergent attacks or defenses.
No ablation or theory on why population-based learning helps.
Code neither provided nor promised.
Requires white-box access to the agent.
Only two small models tested.
Compute resources not reported.
Threat model unrealistic: attacker knows defender's function names.
Injection setup contradicts indirect prompt injection definition (user says follow webpage).
No evaluation on spotlighting dataset or comparison with that defense.
Differences between BrowserGym and AgentDojo not clarified.
Instruction-detection defense mentioned but not compared.
Threat model narrow: random-line injections, leakage-only goal, short episodes.
Claim of easy extension to other risks untested.
Dual-use and release of attacker model not discussed.
Large residual leakage after training under-discussed.
No adaptive-attacker evaluation against frozen agent.
Any-subset string match is a poor proxy for harm.
Diversity claim lacks behavioural rather than embedding-based meaning.
No latency or cost figures for training pipeline.
Wording ('significantly', 'wide range') exceeds evidence; residual leakage high.
Only four attacker models, three weak, evaluated.
No fixed-attack-dataset fine-tuning baseline on same budget.
Figure 4 hard to decode; averages over different row sets.
Test-set size, AgentDojo protocol and final checkpoint not stated.
Typos, possible anonymization leaks, Eq. 2 sign.
Robustness separation exists only against the method's own attacker.
'Significantly lower ASR' and AgentDojo generalization unsupported; tiny deltas, no test.
Population-based learning criticality contradicted by SPAG; ablation attacker strengths inconsistent.
Cumulative diversity rises by construction; no baselines or per-checkpoint values.
Task success gain comes from SFT and in-domain RL, not safety training.
Leakage metric counts any subset; legitimate data use may count as attack.
AgentDojo ASR mapping not stated.
Reward structure is not zero-sum as claimed.
No fixed-injection-dataset fine-tuning baseline.
SFT agent more vulnerable than base, undiscussed.
ASR and TSR averages computed over different rows.
Citation errors for SPAG, DPO and sandboxing.
Eq. 2 sign of clipped term.
What the three seeds vary not stated; many ±0.
Related work omits adversarial-RL safety training, injection defenses and benchmarks.
Population-based learning is a known technique; benefit not isolated.
Diversity of manual/ART attacks never measured for comparison.
SFT attacker relies on hand-written prompt; manual design relocated, not removed.
Citation inaccuracies for SPAG, DPO, sandboxing.
Safety result measured mostly against attackers produced by the method itself.
AgentDojo deltas tiny, no significance test, SPAG matches.
AgentDojo protocol not stated.
Diversity analysis rising by construction; no baselines; embeddings do not show strategies.
PBL ablation changes more than stated; conclusion under-identified.
Per-episode opponent sampling mixes opponent strength into GRPO advantages.
TSR gains confounded with in-domain task training.
No fixed-data or instruction-hierarchy defense baselines.
Hyperparameters, compute, test-task count and seed meaning not stated.
No code link.
Final model choice unspecified.
Eq. 2 sign, inconsistent averages, typos.

P.summary: Task-success improvement claim unsupported; due to imitation learning.
TSR metric conflates leakage with capability.
Benefit of population-based learning not explained or ablated.
Missing existing defense baselines and datasets.

Q.summary: Narrow threat model; extension claims untested.
Robustness wording overstated; residual risk high.
Diversity analysis flawed and lacks baselines.
Evaluated mostly against own or weak attackers.
Evaluation protocol details missing (test size, AgentDojo, final checkpoint).
Population-based learning benefit not isolated or contradicted.
TSR gain confounded with SFT/in-domain training.
